Apollo by the Numbers (NASA NTRS, Orloff 2000)
NASA 'What Was the Saturn V?' - 111 meters (363 feet) tall — dimensions

The Saturn V existed to solve one brutal piece of arithmetic: putting a crew on the Moon means throwing roughly 45 tonnes onto a path out of Earth's gravity, and in 1961 nothing on Earth could throw a fraction of that. So von Braun's Marshall team built the largest machine that had ever flown — five F-1 engines at its base, each the most powerful single-chamber rocket engine ever fired at the time, together burning some thirteen tonnes of propellant every second. Everything about it was sized by the destination, not by what looked reasonable. That it flew thirteen times and never once failed to reach space is the part that still doesn't quite seem possible.

The 110.6 m three-stage rocket that put 24 humans on a translunar trajectory and 12 of them on the lunar surface. Thirteen launches between 1967 and 1973, zero losses on ascent. The most powerful rocket to reach orbit for over five decades until Starship's Super Heavy surpassed it in 2024.
First humans to leave low Earth orbit + orbit the Moon
First humans on another celestial body
First crewed LM flight — Earth-orbit LM separation + rendezvous tests
Full lunar-landing dress rehearsal — LM descended to ~14.4 km altitude
Second crewed Moon landing — pinpoint touchdown 163 m from Surveyor 3
The mission that turned a near-disaster into NASA's most celebrated rescue
Third lunar landing — Apollo 13's lost target reached; Shepard's golf shots
First J-mission — extended stay, first Lunar Roving Vehicle, "Genesis Rock"
Last crewed mission to the Moon (and the only Apollo with a trained geologist)
First Moon landing in the lunar highlands — Descartes; John Young's "lunar Grand Prix"
Launched Apollo 8, 9 and 11–17 (Apollo 9 in Earth orbit; Apollo 10 flew from 39B); today flies Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, and Crew Dragon
First crewed lunar lander; Eagle, Antares, Falcon...
Apollo 10 + Skylab + 53 Shuttle flights; now NASA's SLS / Artemis pad
Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP
1970s NASA outer-planet workhorse — Pioneer 10/11, Helios 1/2, Mariner 9/10, Pioneer Venus
First US human-rated launcher — variant of the Army's Redstone IRBM. Launched Freedom 7 (1961-05-05) and Liberty Bell 7 (1961-07-21)
The most powerful single-chamber engine ever flown
The engine that sent Apollo to the Moon — twice
A complete Saturn V of unflown flight stages, in Rocket Park
SA-500D, the Saturn V dynamic test vehicle
A complete Saturn V of real, unflown stages, at the Apollo/Saturn V Center
S-IC-15, an unflown Saturn V first stage
